target_position: Major Marine Tours is the second large-vessel operator in Seward and THE ONLY LARGE-VESSEL OPERATOR IN THAT HARBOUR THAT IS LOCALLY OWNED. Eight vessels from 36 to 192 passengers. About 60 seasonal employees in Seward, peak hiring January 15 to April 15. Ownership is clean and local, and it is a group rather than a single company: their own page states 'We also own Harbor 360 Hotel, Seward's premier waterfront hotel', and both hotel sites carry the reciprocal sentence 'We also own and operate Major Marine Tours', so Major Marine, Harbor 360 Hotel and Seward Gateway Hotel sit under common local ownership. Their careers page confirms the group shape, 'Employment opportunities are available seasonally in Seward onboard as crew, on-land in our reservations office, and at either of our hotel locations.' PORTS, CORRECTING THE PHASE 1 BRIEF: every product page shows Seward only, and the all-cruises page states verbatim 'We offer multiple cruise options departing from the beautiful harbor town of Seward, Alaska'. The full internal link inventory contains no Whittier page. Third-party listings including a live TripAdvisor entity still carry a Prince William Sound / Whittier entry. INFERENCE: Major Marine currently sells Seward departures only and the Whittier product is legacy. No company statement resolving it was found, so the Whittier question is OPEN and must not be asserted either way. THE PEER GROUP IS MIXED: one competitor is a NYSE-listed Outside corporate, everyone else in the set is Alaskan and privately held.

exposure.gap: Package sales are phone-gated, and the direct competitor sells the same bundle online.
exposure.evidence: Major Marine's specials page states verbatim 'Packages are available to book by phone only unless noted in the package description', reservations office '8:00am - 6:00pm AKST 7 days a week'. Both hotel sites in their own group route the cruise-plus-hotel bundle to the same number, verbatim from Harbor 360, 'To add a Major Marine Tours cruise to your hotel reservation, please call us at (907) 224-8030'. Pursuit's FAQ states bookings can be made 'online, over the phone or in-person', so the multi-product path is not phone-only there.

exposure.gap: Change and cancellation is a phone action with no self-serve path on the site.
exposure.evidence: Refund policy states 'Cruise-only reservations are refundable up to 72 hours prior', a free date change 'up to 24 hours prior to departure', 'Any subsequent change is subject to a $15 per person re-booking fee'. Mechanism given is 'call us at (907) 224-8030'. CONTEXT THAT CUTS BOTH WAYS AND MUST BE CARRIED INTO THE STUDY: no competitor in this set was verified to have self-serve cancellation either. Pursuit routes to a Central Reservations phone line or email. Phillips' own engine has no lookup or modify option. Stan Stephens' Starboard Suite checkout shows none. THIS IS A FIELD-WIDE GAP, NOT A MAJOR MARINE DEFECT.

exposure.gap: The booking stack is opaque from outside, and every other operator in the set has a legible one.
exposure.evidence: Major Marine's booking platform is NOT DETERMINED. Ruled out: FareHarbor under both standard shortnames (HTTP 404), and a reservations or book subdomain (no DNS). Their privacy policy names Google Analytics and DoubleClick and says only that transactions are 'processed through a gateway provider' without naming it. By contrast Phillips runs a self-branded ASP.NET engine, Stan Stephens runs Starboard Suite, and two Seward operators run FareHarbor with the embed URL visible in the href.

exposure.gap: Online booking closes earlier than the direct large-vessel competitor's.
exposure.evidence: Major Marine reservation pages state verbatim 'Online bookings not available within 12 hours of cruise departure - please call us at (907) 224-8030 to book within 12 hours.' Phillips' own engine states 'Cruises can be booked online until 12:00 PM on day of travel.'

exposure.gap: Pricing is published as fixed discounts while the direct competitor states time-based price movement.
exposure.evidence: Major Marine publishes flat rule-based offers, Alaska resident 20 percent, SAVE10 for 10 percent on 2027, 20 percent for repeat 2025 guests. Kenai Fjords Tours states 'prices will increase as the date approaches'. No dynamic or yield-based pricing language was found anywhere on majormarine.com.

exposure.gap: Flexibility is a cost centre here and a product there.
exposure.evidence: Major Marine charges a '$15 per person re-booking fee' for a second change and retains 'A 3% credit card processing fee' on cancellations. Pursuit sells the same flexibility as an upsell, Perk Pass, whose stated benefits include 'Flexible tour date changes and cancellations ($15 value)'.

exposure.gap: The travel trade channel is a manual form against a competitor running an API-documented reseller portal.
exposure.evidence: Major Marine's trade page offers a form with 'Commission' or 'Net Rate' and a phone number. No API, allotment system or distribution platform is named. Pursuit runs affiliates.pursuitcollection.com, 'Powered by Ventrata', with published API documentation and Adyen payments.

exposure.gap: Arrival is a counter transaction with no digital path shown.
exposure.evidence: Check-in page states 'Please check in one hour prior to your cruise departure time for all cruises' and 'All Cruises Depart from Harbor 360 Hotel Office'. No online check-in, mobile ticket or QR code appears.

exposure.gap: No chat, chatbot or AI assistant on the site, with the phone room carrying a 10-hour daily window.
exposure.evidence: Contact page lists only two phone numbers, info@majormarine.com and hours '8:00 a.m. - 6:00 p.m.' seven days a week year-round, with no live chat.

leap_ahead_openings.evidence: Major Marine, 'Please check in one hour prior to your cruise departure time for all cruises'. No online check-in, mobile ticket or QR flow was found on any competitor page fetched.

leap_ahead_openings.evidence: Searches across the Seward, Whittier and Valdez day-cruise field returned no operator press release, product launch or technology statement mentioning AI, chatbots, voice agents or automation. Pursuit's investor material surfaces revenue and EBITDA targets, not an AI programme.

leap_ahead_openings.observation: THE ONE STRUCTURAL ADVANTAGE NOBODY ELSE IN SEWARD HAS IS THE OWNED-LODGING STACK. Major Marine owns the boats, Harbor 360 Hotel and Seward Gateway Hotel, and boards passengers from the Harbor 360 office. Pursuit is the only competitor with a comparable lodging plus tour footprint in Seward, and it is Outside-owned.
leap_ahead_openings.evidence: 'We also own Harbor 360 Hotel' on majormarine.com, the reciprocal 'We also own and operate Major Marine Tours' on both hotel sites, 'either of our hotel locations' on the careers page, and 'All Cruises Depart from Harbor 360 Hotel Office'. Pursuit's Alaska Collection carries Seward Windsong Lodge and Kenai Fjords Wilderness Lodge alongside Kenai Fjords Tours.

where_target_is_behind: Against Pursuit specifically, on three checkable things. Packages are phone-only at Major Marine while Pursuit sells multi-product online. Pursuit states advance-purchase price movement and sells flexibility as a paid Perk Pass while Major Marine publishes flat discount codes and charges a $15 rebooking fee. Pursuit runs an API-documented Ventrata-powered reseller portal while Major Marine's travel trade channel is a commission-or-net-rate inquiry form. Against the smaller Seward operators, Major Marine's booking stack is the only one in the harbour that shows no legible vendor, and its online booking closes 12 hours out where Phillips sells online until noon on the day of travel. AGAINST NOBODY on cancellation self-service, because no operator in this field has it.
where_target_could_lead: The whole field is empty on three fronts at once, verified page by page. No live chat, chatbot or AI assistant anywhere in Seward, Whittier or Valdez day cruising. No customer-facing self-serve cancel or reschedule at any operator, including the NYSE-listed one. No online check-in or mobile boarding pass at any large-vessel operator. Major Marine is also the only Seward operator that owns its boats and two hotels and boards from its own hotel lobby.
thin_spots: MAJOR MARINE'S BOOKING ENGINE IS NOT DETERMINED. Ruled out: FareHarbor under two standard shortnames (404), a reservations or book subdomain (no DNS). Not ruled out: a JavaScript-injected third-party widget the fetcher strips. NEVER STATE A VENDOR.

KENAI FJORDS TOURS' CONSUMER CHECKOUT VENDOR IS INFERENCE, NOT FACT. Ventrata is verified only on Pursuit's reseller portal, and Ventrata's public client list does not name Kenai Fjords Tours. Do not state it as fact.

PHILLIPS' MARKETING SITE WOULD NOT RENDER, so their founder story, fleet numbers from their own mouth, cancellation day-tiers and any chat widget are all unverified. Both policy PDFs fetched as unextractable binary.

SELF-SERVE CANCELLATION IS UNCONFIRMED FOR THE TWO FAREHARBOR OPERATORS. The embeds would not render, and FareHarbor's customer self-cancel is an operator-level setting, so Seward Ocean Excursions and Seacor could have it switched on.
NORTHERN LATITUDE ADVENTURES COULD NOT BE VERIFIED as an operating Whittier or Seward day-cruise company. Not in the competitor set.

MAJOR MARINE'S WHITTIER STATUS IS OPEN. Their own site is Seward-only across the complete internal link inventory. Third-party listings including a live TripAdvisor entity still describe Prince William Sound departures from Whittier. No company statement resolves it.
SEACOR'S CANCELLATION POLICY was not read off a fetched page and is left blank rather than guessed.
ALASKA.ORG'S 'LARGEST FLEET IN SOUTHCENTRAL ALASKA' claim for Kenai Fjords Tours is third-party editorial. Nobody's vessel count was cross-checked against USCG records.
